baseline: Your tests pass on the real RingBuffer

variants.name: front-returns-newest
variants.label: front() returns the newest item instead of the oldest
variants.hint: Push two different values and check front().

variants.name: back-returns-oldest
variants.label: back() returns the oldest item instead of the newest
variants.hint: Check back() too, after two different pushes.

variants.name: pop-does-not-remove
variants.label: pop() returns the oldest item but leaves it in the buffer
variants.hint: What is size() after a pop?

variants.name: full-buffer-drops-the-newest
variants.label: push() onto a full buffer drops the new item instead of overwriting the oldest
variants.hint: Push more items than the capacity and look at what is left.

variants.name: at-ignores-the-start
variants.label: at(i) ignores where the oldest item is, so it is wrong after the buffer wrapped around
variants.hint: at() must count from the oldest item, also after the buffer has wrapped around.

variants.name: pop-empty-returns-garbage
variants.label: pop() on an empty buffer does not throw
variants.hint: What does the documentation promise for pop() on an empty buffer?

variants.name: at-allows-size
variants.label: at(size()) does not throw (an off-by-one)
variants.hint: Test the index just beyond the last item, and the last valid one.

variants.name: full-one-too-early
variants.label: full() reports true one item too early
variants.hint: full() is true when the buffer holds exactly `capacity` items: test just below and exactly at the capacity, for several capacities.

variants.name: zero-capacity-allowed
variants.label: a buffer of capacity 0 is accepted
variants.hint: The constructor must reject a capacity of 0.
